raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The three DSA metadata kernels (`_fused_dsa_decode_metadata_kernel`, `_fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata_kernel`, `_fused_dsa_draft_extend_metadata_kernel`) take the batch size as a `tl.constexpr`. They run outside CUDA graphs on every decode, verify and draft step, and the batch size changes whenever a request joins or finishes. So a server compiles each kernel again for every new batch size, up to `--max-running-requests` times, while it serves. Each compile stalls every request on the server.

The kernels use the batch size only in masks (`offs_b < bs`, `row < bs`, `out_row < expanded_size`) and as the bound of `tl.range` loops. None of these needs a compile-time value. `BLOCK_BS` and `BLOCK_EXPANDED` (powers of two) already set the tile shapes.

## Modifications

- `dsa_metadata.py`: `bs` is a runtime argument in the three kernels, and `expanded_size = bs * next_n` is a runtime value in the target-verify kernel. The launchers are unchanged. The kernels now compile once per `BLOCK_BS` / `BLOCK_EXPANDED` pair (Triton still specializes the integer on 1 and on multiples of 16).
- `test_dsa_metadata.py`: `test_decode_does_not_recompile_for_each_batch_size` runs the decode kernel for batch sizes 5, 6 and 7 (one `BLOCK_BS`) and checks that the second and third sizes add no compiled kernel.

## Accuracy Tests

The kernels compute the same values: only the compile-time status of `bs` changes. All existing tests of `test_dsa_metadata.py` compare each kernel with an eager reference with `rtol=0, atol=0`, and they pass with the change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On one B200 node, GLM-5.3-Flash (FP8, DSA k-pool, MTP), TP8, v0.5.20 with this change backported, empty Triton cache:

- Without the change, the first decode batch of each new size added about 0.5 s: rounds of 7 and 12 concurrent sampled requests (64 output tokens each) took 1.99 s and 1.91 s, and their repeats 1.45 s and 1.36 s. The repeats were still slow, because the batch size shrinks as requests finish and each smaller size compiles again.
- With the change and a start-up warmup of one batch size per `BLOCK_BS` bucket, the same rounds took 1.12 s and 1.36 s, the same as their repeats (1.07 s and 1.25 s).
- Steady-state decode did not change: time per verify step was 0.999x, 1.006x and 1.002x of the server without the change with 1, 4 and 16 requests in flight.

## Validation

```bash
python3 -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_metadata.py
```

- On B200 (Triton 3.7.1), the test file was run against `main` and against this branch. On `main` the new test fails with `AssertionError: 3 != 1` (three compiled kernels for three batch sizes). With this change all 9 tests pass.
- `pre-commit run --files` passes for the two changed files.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no user-facing change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

When the supported CUDA k-pool path is used (for example GLM-5.3 with `index_kpool=4` and page size 64), `SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_DSA_KPOOL_METADATA_FUSION` defaults to true (`environ.py:1729`) and `_init_kpool_metadata_fusion` replaces all three ordinary wrappers changed here with functions from `dsa_kpool_metadata` (`dsa_metadata_manager.py:41-70`). @@ -30,7 +30,7 @@ def _fused_dsa_decode_metadata_kernel(
     page_table_stride_1: tl.constexpr,
     real_page_table_stride_0,
     real_page_table_stride_1: tl.constexpr,
-    bs: tl.constexpr,
+    bs,
     max_len,
     dsa_index_topk: tl.constexpr,
     physical_page_size: tl.constexpr,
@@ -231,7 +231,7 @@ def _fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata_kernel(
     real_page_table_stride_1: tl.constexpr,
     paged_mqa_ctx_lens_stride_0: tl.constexpr,
     paged_mqa_ctx_lens_stride_1: tl.constexpr,
-    bs: tl.constexpr,
+    bs,
     max_seqlen_k,
     dsa_index_topk: tl.constexpr,
     physical_page_size: tl.constexpr,
@@ -244,7 +244,7 @@ def _fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata_kernel(
     BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
 ):
     pid = tl.program_id(0)
-    expanded_size: tl.constexpr = bs * next_n
+    expanded_size = bs * next_n
 
     if pid == 0:
         offs_b = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_BS)
@@ -473,7 +473,7 @@ def _fused_dsa_draft_extend_metadata_kernel(
     page_table_stride_1: tl.constexpr,
     real_page_table_stride_0,
     real_page_table_stride_1: tl.constexpr,
-    bs: tl.constexpr,
+    bs,
     total_len,
     max_seqlen_k,
     dsa_index_topk: tl.constexpr,

@@ -3,6 +3,7 @@
 import torch
 
 from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa_metadata import (
+    _fused_dsa_decode_metadata_kernel,
     fused_dsa_decode_metadata,
     fused_dsa_draft_extend_metadata,
     fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata,
@@ -499,6 +500,24 @@ def test_large_shape_coverage(self):
             static_extend_len=True,
         )
 
+    def test_decode_does_not_recompile_for_each_batch_size(self):
+        # The kernel runs outside CUDA graphs on every decode step, and the batch
+        # size changes whenever a request joins or finishes. Batch sizes with the
+        # same BLOCK_BS must reuse one compiled kernel.
+        kernel_cache = _fused_dsa_decode_metadata_kernel.device_caches[
+            self.device.index or 0
+        ][0]
+        for bs in (5, 6, 7):
+            self._check_decode(
+                list(range(9, 9 + bs)),
+                max_len=97,
+                dsa_index_topk=64,
+                physical_page_size=1,
+            )
+            if bs == 5:
+                compiled_after_first = len(kernel_cache)
+        self.assertEqual(len(kernel_cache), compiled_after_first)
+
     def test_large_batch_coverage(self):
         bs = 16 * 1024
         seq_lens = (torch.arange(bs, dtype=torch.int64) % 257 + 1).tolist()
